artworks.title: The Fall of the Giants (Sistine Chapel)
artworks.description: On the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel, Michelangelo stages the Gigantomachy as naked colossi hurled from heaven by the wrath of Olympian gods — the visual tradition Apollodorus compresses into named duels at Phlegra, where Heracles the mortal ally was required before any Giant could fall.

artworks.title: The Gigantomachy frieze of the Pergamon Altar
artworks.description: Berlin's Pergamonmuseum frieze: Olympians storm the serpent-legged Gigantes with boulders and torches — the most ambitious surviving ancient Gigantomachy, the Attalids' allegory of cosmic and barbarian defeat.

artworks.title: The Fall of the Giants (Sala dei Giganti)
artworks.description: Mantua's Palazzo Te: Zeus hurls thunderbolts while Giants are crushed beneath collapsing mountains — Mannerist illusion that makes the whole room cave in on the viewer.

artworks.title: Olympus: The Fall of the Giants
artworks.description: Bayeu's Spanish Baroque canvas: the Giants tumble from Olympus as Zeus's lightning clears the mountain — the earthborn revolt restaged for an eighteenth-century ceiling imagination.

artworks.title: Attic black-figure neck-amphora: Athena intervening in the Gigantomachy
artworks.description: Vatican amphora: Athena strides into the duel as Olympians close on the Gigantes — sixth-century Athenian pottery that echoes the peplos woven with the Gigantomachy for the Panathenaia.
